newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-St Barbara says Atkins in proceedings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-St Barbara says Atkins in proceedings.

text.p: St Barbara Mines Ltd, which has said it wants to merge with Mt Leyshon Mines Ltd, said on Monday interests associated with major shareholder Ross Atkins had sought a court order blocking the plan.
St Barbara said the action was taken with a view to restraining St Barbara from despatching its formal takeover documents to Mt Leyshon. Both companies are gold miners.

"Other orders are also sought, including damages and cancellation of the proposed takeover offer," St Barbara said in a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange. St Barbara said it and its directors would defend the action.

St Barbara said the Supreme Court of Western Australia would hear an application on Tuesday for an interlocutory injunction restraining the company from despatching its formal "Part A" statement. "As soon as the court's decision is known, the market will be informed," St Barbara said.
Atkins, jointly with former chairman Alan Birchmore, controls 47.2 percent of St Barbara. He was unseated as the regional director of St Barbara in October 1995.

St Barbara has said the offer would be 32 of its shares for each 10 Mt Leyshon shares. Normandy Mining Ltd, which controls 76 percent of Mt Leyshon, has not said whether it will accept the offer, which is subject to 75-percent acceptances.
St Barbara shares closed two cents higher at 71 cents on Monday while Mt Leyshon closed 10 cents weaker at A$2.10.

The two companies have a combined market capitalisation of about A$315 million at current prices. A successful merger would create a company with annual gold production of about 350,000 ounces and a resource base of about 4.8 million ounces.
